nodeData.note: How to count the goods a business holds, compare the count with the books, sort out the differences, and put the right value on the stock. Written for people already doing it at work, with a duka and a pharmacy example.

children.note: A stock take is a physical count of every item the business holds for sale or use. You count it, check its condition, and compare the result with what the records say.
Going round the shelves and store and counting every item by hand or scanner, on one date. It proves what is really there.

manas.q: What is a stock take?

children.note: Goods held to sell, goods being made, and materials used to make them. In a duka it is soap, sugar and airtime; in a pharmacy, medicines.

manas.q: What is inventory?

children.note: Closing stock goes on the balance sheet and lowers cost of sales. A wrong count means wrong profit, so the count must be right.
Theft, breakage, expiry and record errors only show up when you count. The sooner you know, the sooner you can stop the leak.
If you use stock software (a perpetual system), the count tests whether the system's numbers can be trusted.

manas.q: What is a perpetual inventory system?

children.note: Auditors, banks and SACCO lenders want proof that the stock in the accounts exists and is worth what you say.

children.topic: Periodic system: count gives cost of sales
children.note: With no running stock records, cost of sales = opening stock + purchases − closing stock. Example: 80,000 + 420,000 − 95,000 = KES 405,000.

manas.q: How is cost of sales found under a periodic system?

children.note: Most count problems come from poor planning. Plan two to four weeks ahead for a full count.
Usually the year-end date, or as close to it as possible. Pick a quiet time, such as after closing or on a Sunday.
One or two pages telling everyone how to count, where to write, what to do with damaged goods and who to ask. Give them out before the day.

manas.q: Why issue written count instructions?

children.note: Draw a simple plan of shelves, store rooms and fridges and give each area a code. Every area gets a team and a sheet.
One person counts, one writes and checks. Where possible, at least one person should not be the usual storekeeper.

manas.q: Why count in teams of two?

children.note: Sheets or tags with printed serial numbers. Record which numbers each team gets and make sure every one comes back, even if spoiled.

manas.q: Why are count sheets pre-numbered?

children.note: Mark goods held for customers, supplier consignment stock and returns waiting collection. Count them separately so they are not added to your stock.
Cut-off means the count and the books must agree on the same moment in time. Goods move every day, so you draw a line.
Every receipt and sale up to the count time is in both the count and the books; nothing after it is in either.

manas.q: What is cut-off in a stock take?

children.note: Stop receiving and issuing goods during the count. If you must keep trading, put new deliveries aside and count them separately.
Write down the last goods received note (GRN), last delivery note and last sales invoice before the count. Later, check the books stop at the same numbers.

manas.q: Why record the last GRN and invoice numbers?

children.note: If the sale is already invoiced, the goods belong to the customer. Do not include them in your count.
Goods on the road may or may not be yours. It depends on the delivery terms; check who owns them at the count date.
The count itself: careful, steady and documented.
Counters are not shown the system quantity. They write what they see, so they are not tempted to match the book figure.

manas.q: What is a blind count?

children.note: Once an area is done, stick a mark or tag on it. This stops items being missed or counted twice.
Write the unit you counted, such as single bottles, packs of 10 or cartons of 24. Mixing units is a top cause of big errors.
Write down damaged, expired, near-expiry and slow-moving items on the sheet. They may need a lower value later.
A supervisor recounts a sample. Pick some from the sheet and find them on the shelf, and some on the shelf and find them on the sheet.

manas.q: What are the two directions of test counts?

children.note: If a test count or a big variance shows a gap, recount that area with a different team before anyone leaves.
Check every numbered sheet is back, signed by both counters and the supervisor. Make copies before anyone types them in.
Stock that cannot be sold at full price must be valued lower. The count is the best time to spot it.
Items with few or no sales for months. Compare the count with sales history to find them.
Past its use-by date and cannot legally be sold, common in pharmacies and food shops. Usually written down to nil and disposed of properly.
Still sellable but only at a discount soon. It may need a write-down to what you can now sell it for.
Broken packs, old models or out-of-fashion goods. Value at what they can be sold for, less costs to sell.
After the count, compare item by item with the system. The difference is the variance, and each big one must be explained.
Counted quantity minus system quantity. Negative means stock is missing; positive means more than the books show.

manas.q: What is a stock variance?

children.note: Multiply the unit difference by unit cost. Look into the biggest values first, not just the biggest unit counts.
Sales or receipts not recorded, items keyed to the wrong product code, unit mix-ups, cut-off errors, damage and theft.
Check delivery notes, sales records and recounts first. Only post a loss when you cannot find a record error.
Stock that is gone without a record, through theft, damage or error. It is a cost to the business.

manas.q: What is shrinkage?

children.note: A manager signs off the final variance list before the system is adjusted. This stops staff hiding their own losses.
Invented businesses with KES figures. Check each journal: debits equal credits.
Mama Neema's duka counts at closing on 31 March. Two items differ from the system.
System 40, counted 37. Cost KES 250 each, so short 3 × 250 = KES 750.
System 24, counted 25. Cost KES 380, so over by KES 380. A sale was keyed as oil instead of another item.
−750 + 380 = KES 370 short overall. Fix the mis-keyed sale first, then look at the sugar.
System stock at cost KES 186,400. Count at cost KES 182,150. Gap KES 4,250 short.
A supplier invoice for KES 1,800 was posted twice. Dr Trade payables 1,800 / Cr Inventory 1,800.
4,250 − 1,800 = KES 2,450 unexplained. Dr Stock losses (cost of sales) 2,450 / Cr Inventory 2,450.
186,400 − 1,800 − 2,450 = 182,150, which matches the count. Each journal has equal debits and credits.
Afya Plus Pharmacy finds 30 packs of an expired antibiotic, cost KES 320 each, at the year-end count.
30 × 320 = KES 9,600. Expired medicine cannot be sold, so its value is nil.
Dr Expired stock written off (cost of sales) 9,600 / Cr Inventory 9,600. Keep the disposal record for the regulator and audit.
12 bottles with stained boxes. Cost KES 450 each. Can sell for KES 300 each, with KES 20 a bottle in selling costs.
300 − 20 = KES 280. This is less than cost of 450, so value at 280.
(450 − 280) × 12 = 170 × 12 = KES 2,040. Dr Inventory write-down (cost of sales) 2,040 / Cr Inventory 2,040.

children.topic: Cost vs NRV: item by item
children.note: Three product lines in a hardware shop. Compare each line separately.
Total cost 98,000; value 50,000 + 24,000 + 18,000 = KES 92,000. Write-down KES 6,000: Dr Cost of sales 6,000 / Cr Inventory 6,000.
Total NRV is 104,500, above cost of 98,000, so a total check shows no loss. That hides the KES 6,000 loss on line B.
IAS 2 Inventories sets how to value stock. IFRS for SMEs, used by many small Kenyan firms, has the same main idea.
Stock goes in the books at whichever is lower: what it cost, or what you can get for it (net realisable value).

manas.q: How does IAS 2 measure inventory?

children.note: Expected selling price, less any costs to finish the item, less the costs of selling it.

manas.q: What is net realisable value?

children.note: Purchase price, import duties you cannot recover, and transport to bring goods in. Plus conversion costs if you make the goods.

manas.q: What is included in the cost of inventory?

children.note: Selling costs, abnormal waste, general office costs and storage that is not part of making the goods. These are expenses.

manas.q: Which costs are excluded from inventory cost?

children.note: Use first in, first out (FIFO) or weighted average cost. LIFO is not allowed under IAS 2.

manas.q: Which cost formulas does IAS 2 allow?

children.note: Compare cost and NRV for each item or close group of items, not for all stock in one total.

manas.q: Should cost and NRV be compared in total or item by item?

children.topic: Write-down goes to cost of sales
children.note: A fall to NRV is an expense in the period it happens. If NRV later rises, the write-down can be reversed, up to original cost.
You can count everything once a year, or count a small part every week so all of it is covered over the year.
Everything counted on one day, usually at year end. Simple, but trading often has to stop.

manas.q: What is a full (wall-to-wall) count?

children.note: A few items counted on a regular rota, so the whole store is covered over time. Needs a good perpetual system.

manas.q: What is a cycle count?

children.topic: ABC: count the costly items more
children.note: Group items by value. A items (high value or fast-moving) are counted often, C items (cheap, slow) less often.

manas.q: What is ABC analysis in cycle counting?

children.note: No big shutdown, errors found sooner, and staff get used to counting well.
Only if the system is reliable and the counts are well run and recorded. Otherwise a year-end full count is still needed.
When stock is material, the external auditor usually comes to watch the count. ISA 501 covers this.
When inventory is material, the auditor should attend the count if practical, to see that stock exists and is in good condition.

manas.q: Which ISA covers attending the inventory count?

children.note: Whether staff follow the count instructions, keep cut-off, and separate damaged and other people's goods.
The auditor counts a sample both ways (sheet to floor and floor to sheet) and keeps a record to check later against the final list.
The auditor notes the last GRN and dispatch numbers to test cut-off in the books afterwards.
Watch for these at work and in exams.
Turns the count into a tick exercise. Use blind counts.

manas.q: Why should counters not see system quantities?

children.note: Writing 10 when it was 10 cartons of 24. Always write the unit of measure.
Invoiced goods awaiting collection or supplier consignment stock are not yours. Leave them out.
Gains on some lines hide losses on others. Always compare item by item.
A variance may be a record error. Investigate first, or you hide a real problem.
Try each question before opening the answer steps.
120 units cost KES 800 each. Selling price KES 900, selling costs KES 150 a unit. Value and write-down?
900 − 150 = KES 750 per unit, below cost of 800.
Value 120 × 750 = KES 90,000. Cost 120 × 800 = 96,000. Write-down KES 6,000: Dr Cost of sales 6,000 / Cr Inventory 6,000.
System shows 2,500 units; count finds 2,440. Unit cost KES 150. No record error found. Journal?
Dr Stock losses (cost of sales) 9,000 / Cr Inventory 9,000. Both sides KES 9,000.
Count at cost KES 610,000 includes goods costing KES 30,000 already sold and invoiced, waiting for collection. Correct stock?
The sale is invoiced, so the goods belong to the customer and must be left out.

nodeData.note: Credit control is how a business decides who may buy now and pay later, and then makes sure they really pay. Good credit control turns sales into cash on time. Bad debts and allowances were taught in CA11; here we use them at work.

children.topic: What it is and why cash matters
children.note: Selling on credit wins customers, but a sale is not cash until the customer pays.
Credit control means giving credit carefully and collecting what customers owe on time. It covers the whole path from a new customer to the money in the bank.

manas.q: What is credit control?

children.note: Money customers owe for goods or services already given is called trade receivables, or debtors. It is an asset in the statement of financial position.

manas.q: What are trade receivables (debtors)?

children.note: A business can show a profit and still fail to pay rent and salaries if customers pay late. Cash pays the bills, not profit on paper.
Money stuck with customers may force you to borrow, pay interest, or delay paying your own suppliers. The longer a debt is unpaid, the less likely it is to be paid at all.
Decide the rules before you give credit, write them down, and tell the customer.
Credit terms say how long the customer has to pay, for example 30 days from the invoice date. Put them on the account form and on every invoice.

manas.q: What are credit terms?

children.note: A credit limit is the most a customer may owe you at any one time. New orders above the limit wait until the customer pays down the balance.

manas.q: What is a credit limit?

children.note: Give a new customer a low limit. Raise it only after months of paying on time.
Some firms offer a small discount for paying early. It speeds up cash but costs money, so compare the cost with the benefit. See CA11 for how discounts are recorded.
A short policy sets out who approves credit, the normal terms, the reminder steps and when to stop supplies. Everyone then follows the same rules.
Know who you are dealing with before you give credit.
Collect the legal name, KRA PIN, physical address, phone, owners' names and who will pay invoices. Ask the customer to sign your terms.
Ask for two suppliers who already give the customer credit. Call them and ask how much credit they give and whether the customer pays on time.

manas.q: What is a trade reference?

children.note: A bank can confirm the account exists and how it is run, usually with the customer's written consent.
A credit bureau collects records of how people and firms repay debts and sells reports to lenders. In Kenya these are called credit reference bureaus (CRBs).

manas.q: What does a credit reference bureau do?

children.note: Metropol Credit Reference Bureau is based in Nairobi and also works in Rwanda, Tanzania and Uganda. Check which bureaus are licensed today before you sign up.
For a bigger limit, ask for recent financial statements. Look at cash, profit and how much they already owe others.
The payment clock starts with the invoice, so send it fast and get it right.
Raise the invoice when goods leave or the job is done. A late invoice means late cash.
Invoice number and date, customer name, delivery note or order number, items, prices, total due, due date and how to pay (bank or M-Pesa paybill and account number).
KRA requires businesses to issue tax invoices through its eTIMS system. Rules and who must comply change, so check the current KRA rules.
A wrong price or missing order number gives the customer a reason to wait. Check the invoice before it goes out.
This report shows who owes what, and for how long. It is the credit controller's daily tool.
An aged receivables (aged debtors) report lists each customer's balance split by how old the unpaid invoices are. The row totals and the column totals both add up to total receivables.

manas.q: What is an aged receivables (aged debtors) report?

children.note: Common bands are current (0–30 days), 31–60 days, 61–90 days and over 90 days. Older bands carry more risk.
Start with the oldest and largest balances. Note any customer over their limit, and watch good payers who suddenly slow down.
The report total must agree with the trade receivables control account in the ledger. A difference means a posting error.
A fixed, polite routine collects most debts. Be firm, friendly and consistent.
A short reminder a few days before the due date prevents many late payments.
A statement lists the opening balance, invoices, payments and the closing balance. Send it every month so the customer can agree their balance.

manas.q: What is a customer statement?

children.note: Send a reminder once a debt is overdue, then call. Ask for a date and an amount, write it down, and follow up on that date.
Give a business paybill or till number and tell the customer what account reference to use, such as the invoice number. This makes matching payments easy.
Match each payment to the invoices it pays. Unmatched cash makes the aged report wrong and causes arguments.
If a customer is well overdue or over the limit, put the account on hold. No new deliveries until it is brought up to date.

manas.q: What does putting an account on stop mean?

children.note: Record every call and promise with date and name. It helps the next person and is evidence if the matter goes further.
Some customers do not pay because something went wrong. Find out quickly.
Wrong price, short delivery, damaged goods or a missing order number. Ask early: "Is there any reason this invoice cannot be paid?"
Check the delivery note and order. If you are wrong, issue a credit note; if you are right, send the proof.
Ask the customer to pay the parts not in dispute now. One small problem should not hold up the whole balance.
When a debt will not be paid, the books must show it. CA11 covers the rules; IFRS 9 (taught in CA23) sets the model.
A bad debt is one you are sure will never be paid, for example the customer has closed and cannot be found. You remove it from receivables.

manas.q: What is a bad debt?

children.note: Dr Bad debts expense; Cr Trade receivables. The expense goes to profit or loss and the asset falls.

manas.q: What is the journal to write off a bad debt?

children.note: An allowance is an estimate of debts that may not be paid. It sits against receivables so the net figure is what you expect to collect.

manas.q: What is an allowance for doubtful debts?

children.note: Increase: Dr Bad debts expense; Cr Allowance. Decrease: Dr Allowance; Cr Bad debts expense. Only the change goes through profit or loss.

manas.q: How do you record an increase in the allowance for doubtful debts?

children.topic: Expected credit loss in plain words
children.note: IFRS 9 asks you to set the allowance at the losses you expect, using past experience and what you know now, not only debts already in trouble. Older debts get higher loss rates.

manas.q: What does IFRS 9 expected credit loss mean in plain words?

children.note: If a written-off debt is later paid: Dr Bank; Cr Bad debts recovered (income), or reverse the expense.
Receivable days tell you how long, on average, customers take to pay.
Receivable days = trade receivables ÷ credit sales × 365. Use credit sales only, not cash sales.

manas.q: What is the formula for receivable days?

children.note: If terms are 30 days and receivable days are 45, customers are paying about 15 days late on average.
Rising receivable days month after month is an early warning. Look at the aged report to see which customers cause it.
A big sale just before year-end raises receivables and makes the ratio look worse. Read the number with the business story.
When the routine fails, escalate step by step. Get proper legal advice before going to court.
A formal letter states the amount, gives a short final deadline and says what you will do next. Keep a copy and proof of delivery.

manas.q: What is a demand letter?

children.note: Kenya has a Small Claims Court, set up under the Small Claims Court Act of 2016, for simpler civil money claims such as unpaid contracts. Check the current claim limit and fees with the Judiciary.
A debt collection agency chases the debt for a fee, often a share of what it collects. Agree the fee in writing and check how they treat customers.
Chasing a small debt can cost more than the debt. Sometimes writing it off is the sensible choice.
Mwangaza Hardware Wholesalers is an invented Nairobi hardware wholesaler. It sells cement, iron sheets and tools on 30-day terms.
Total owed at 31 October: KES 450,000. The rows and columns below both add to this.
All current: 50,000. Nothing overdue.
Call Jua Kali Welders about the 35,000 over 90 days and put them on stop. Then call Kilimo Fundi about the 30,000 at 61–90 days.
Credit sales for the year: KES 3,650,000. Receivables: KES 450,000.
Terms are 30 days, so customers pay about 15 days late on average. The overdue bands in the aged report explain why.
Jua Kali Welders has closed and the owner cannot be found. The 35,000 over 90 days will not be paid.
Dr Bad debts expense KES 35,000; Cr Trade receivables KES 35,000. Debits 35,000 = credits 35,000.
450,000 − 35,000 = 415,000. The aged table now shows current 250,000; 31–60 days 120,000; 61–90 days 45,000; over 90 nil, which adds to 415,000.
Past experience gives loss rates of 1% for current, 5% for 31–60 days and 20% for 61–90 days. The allowance already in the books is KES 12,000.
Needed 17,500 less existing 12,000 = increase of 5,500. Dr Bad debts expense KES 5,500; Cr Allowance for doubtful debts KES 5,500.
Trade receivables 415,000 less allowance 17,500 = KES 397,500, what Mwangaza expects to collect.
Baraka Builders pays the KES 80,000 in the 31–60 days band through the paybill, quoting the invoice number.
Dr Bank (M-Pesa) KES 80,000; Cr Trade receivables KES 80,000. Debits equal credits.
415,000 − 80,000 = 335,000. Baraka now owes only its current 120,000.

nodeData.note: How a bookkeeper or accountant in a small or medium Kenyan business gets ready for the yearly external audit: what the auditors want, when, how to tidy the books first, and what to do after.

children.note: An independent accountant checks your year-end accounts and gives an opinion on them. Knowing what they look for makes the work faster and cheaper.
An outside, independent auditor checks the financial statements and says whether they give a true and fair view.

manas.q: What is an external audit, in simple words?

children.note: The accounts show the business's results and position honestly, with no big (material) errors, following the accounting rules, often IFRS for SMEs.

manas.q: What does 'true and fair view' mean?

children.note: The end product of the audit: a signed report saying whether the accounts are fairly stated. The auditor gives an opinion, not a guarantee.

manas.q: What is the main output of an external audit?

children.note: Auditors test samples, not every transaction. They aim for high but not total confidence that there is no material error.

manas.q: What level of assurance does an audit give?

children.topic: Material means big enough to matter
children.note: An error is material if it could change the decisions of people reading the accounts. Auditors set a materiality amount at planning.

manas.q: What is a material misstatement?

children.note: Companies that must be audited under the Companies Act, 2015 need an auditor each year. Check which rules apply to your company with your auditor or ICPAK.
Banks, SACCOs, donors, KRA and shareholders trust audited accounts more. A clean audit makes loans and tenders easier.
External auditors are outsiders reporting to shareholders. Internal auditors are staff who check controls during the year. See also CA24 Auditing and Assurance.
Auditors follow International Standards on Auditing (ISAs), issued by the IAASB. You do not need to know them deeply, but these six explain what auditors will ask you for.
Sets the auditor's main goal: get reasonable assurance that the accounts are free of material error, then report. Also asks for professional scepticism.

manas.q: What does ISA 200 cover?

children.note: The auditor plans the strategy and the detailed plan before testing. This is why they ask for a planning meeting and early documents.

manas.q: Which ISA covers planning an audit?

children.note: The auditor must collect enough reliable evidence (sufficient and appropriate) to support the opinion. Your documents are that evidence.

manas.q: What does ISA 500 require?

children.note: The auditor writes directly to banks, customers, suppliers or lenders to confirm balances. Replies go straight to the auditor, not through you.

manas.q: Which ISA covers external confirmations such as bank letters?

children.note: Near the end, management signs a letter confirming key facts, for example that all liabilities and records were given to the auditor.

manas.q: What is a written representation letter (ISA 580)?

children.note: Explains how the auditor decides and writes the opinion. A clean opinion is called unmodified.

manas.q: Which ISA covers forming the audit opinion?

children.note: Unmodified (clean); qualified (fine except for one issue); adverse (accounts are wrong overall); disclaimer (auditor could not get enough evidence).

manas.q: What are the four types of audit opinion?

children.note: An audit runs in stages over several months. Put the dates in your diary early so year-end work is not rushed.
The auditor and the directors agree in writing the scope, fees and duties of each side. Read it so you know what you must provide.
Before year-end, meet the audit senior: discuss changes in the business, new loans, systems, and agree dates and the PBC list.

manas.q: What happens at the audit planning meeting?

children.note: Optional visit before year-end to test controls and early months, such as payroll and purchases. It lightens the final work.
On the last day, count stock (auditors may attend), note the last delivery and invoice numbers, and print bank and M-Pesa statements.
After you close the books, auditors test balances and transactions using your PBC documents. Expect daily queries.

manas.q: What is audit fieldwork?

children.note: Auditors share proposed adjustments and open points. You agree, post the journals, and send updated accounts.
Directors approve the accounts and sign the representation letter; then the auditor signs the report, dated the same day or soon after.
Soon after, the auditor writes to management listing control weaknesses found and suggested fixes.

manas.q: What is a management letter?

children.topic: The PBC list: what to prepare
children.note: PBC means 'prepared by client': the list of schedules and documents the auditor asks you to have ready. Each schedule should agree to the trial balance.
Prepared by client: documents and schedules you, not the auditor, prepare. Having them complete on day one is the biggest time saver.

manas.q: What does PBC stand for in an audit?

children.note: Final year-end trial balance and draft financial statements, with last year's figures beside them for comparison.
Full ledger export for the year, in Excel, so auditors can sample. See also Accounting software and Excel for accountants.
Year-end bank reconciliation for every account, with the bank statements. Auditors also send bank confirmation letters (ISA 505).

manas.q: What bank documents go on the PBC list?

children.note: Till and paybill statements for the year, reconciled to the ledger. See also M-Pesa reconciliation.
Register that agrees to the ledger, with additions (invoices), disposals and depreciation. See also Fixed asset register.
Signed count sheets, the stock valuation and a note of slow or damaged items. See also Stock take.
Aged list of who owes you, agreeing to the ledger, with customer statements and notes on doubtful debts. See also Credit control.
Aged list of what you owe, with supplier statements reconciled to your ledger.
Payroll reports for the year and proof that PAYE and other statutory deductions were filed and paid. See also Running payroll.
Draft tax computation, VAT and other returns with iTax acknowledgement receipts and payment slips. See also Filing returns on iTax and eTIMS invoicing.
Key contracts, leases, loan and overdraft agreements, and lender statements showing the year-end balance and interest.
Minutes of directors' and shareholders' meetings for the year and up to the audit date. They show big decisions auditors must know about.

children.topic: Tidy up before the auditors come
children.note: Most audit adjustments are things you could have found yourself. Do a careful month-end close for the last month. See also Month-end close.
Every asset and liability on the trial balance should have a schedule that agrees to it to the shilling.

manas.q: What should support each balance sheet line before an audit?

children.note: Investigate suspense accounts, old unpresented cheques and unmatched receipts; post correcting journals with a reason.
Year-end journals for accruals, prepayments, depreciation and stock. Keep a numbered list with the support for each one.

manas.q: What is a tidy-up journal?

children.note: Sales and purchases must fall in the right year: match the last delivery notes and invoices before and after year-end.

manas.q: What is cut-off in an audit?

children.note: Put this year and last year side by side. Explain any big jump or drop before the auditor asks.
These are the adjustments auditors propose most often in small businesses, and how to avoid each one.
Bills for the year that arrive after year-end are left out. Avoid: check invoices received in the first weeks after year-end.

manas.q: How do you avoid missing accruals?

children.note: Rent or insurance paid ahead is all put to expense. Avoid: split any payment that covers months in the next year.
A sale or purchase is booked in the wrong year. Avoid: match delivery notes to invoices around the year-end date.
New assets are left off the register, so no depreciation. Avoid: update the register monthly from asset invoices.
Bank charges, direct receipts or reversals are not in the cash book. Avoid: reconcile every month, not only at year-end.
Old debts that will not be paid are still shown in full. Avoid: review the ageing and allow for debts unlikely to be collected.
Five real-style audit fixes for an invented firm, Jua Kali Hardware Ltd, year ending 31 December 2026. Amounts in KES, excluding VAT.
Cash book shows KES 412,000; bank statement shows KES 475,500 at 31 December.

Unpresented cheques KES 86,000 (cheque 1021 KES 50,000, cheque 1024 KES 36,000). Uncredited deposit KES 30,000. Bank charges KES 2,500 and a direct customer transfer of KES 10,000 are not in the cash book.
412,000 − 2,500 + 10,000 = KES 419,500. Journals: Dr Bank charges 2,500 / Cr Bank 2,500; Dr Bank 10,000 / Cr Trade receivables 10,000.
475,500 − 86,000 unpresented + 30,000 uncredited = KES 419,500. Both sides agree, so the reconciliation is done.
The December electricity bill of KES 48,000 arrived on 10 January and was not recorded.
Dr Electricity expense KES 48,000 / Cr Accruals KES 48,000. The cost belongs to the year it was used.
Profit falls by KES 48,000 and liabilities rise by KES 48,000.
On 1 April 2026 the firm paid KES 360,000 rent for 12 months (April 2026 to March 2027) and expensed it all.
Dr Prepayments KES 90,000 / Cr Rent expense KES 90,000. Profit rises by KES 90,000.
An invoice for KES 120,000 (cost KES 80,000) was booked on 31 December, but the goods left on 3 January and were counted in closing stock.
The customer only got the goods in January, so the sale belongs to 2027. The stock count already includes the goods, so cost of sales is right.
Dr Revenue KES 120,000 / Cr Trade receivables KES 120,000. Profit falls by KES 120,000; the KES 80,000 stock stays in closing stock.
A machine bought 1 April 2026 for KES 1,200,000 was never added to the register. Policy: straight line over 5 years, nil residual value.
Dr Depreciation expense KES 180,000 / Cr Accumulated depreciation, plant KES 180,000.
Draft profit KES 2,500,000 − 2,500 − 48,000 + 90,000 − 120,000 − 180,000 = KES 2,239,500. Each journal balanced, so the trial balance still balances.
A smooth audit is mostly good organisation and quick replies. It also keeps the audit fee from growing.
Name one person to receive all requests and track them, so nothing is lost or answered twice.

manas.q: Why name one contact person for the audit?

children.note: One shared folder, with sub-folders numbered to match the PBC list. Name files clearly, for example '04 Bank rec Dec 2026'.
Reply within a day where you can. Slow answers mean more days on site and higher fees.
If you know of an error, tell the auditor early. Hidden problems found later damage trust and delay signing.
The audit ends with signed accounts and a management letter. Use both to make next year easier.
Post every agreed audit journal in your system so your opening balances next year agree to the signed accounts.

manas.q: Why must audit adjustments be posted in your own books?

children.note: It lists weaknesses such as missing approvals or late reconciliations, with a risk rating and the auditor's advice.

children.topic: Agree a fix and a date
children.note: For each point write management's reply, who will fix it and by when. Auditors will check next year.

children.topic: Fix the weakness, not just the error
children.note: If bank reconciliations were late, set a monthly deadline and a reviewer, so the same error does not come back.
Traps that slow audits down and raise fees.

children.topic: Schedules not agreeing to the TB
children.note: A debtors list that is KES 15,000 off the ledger wastes hours. Always agree each schedule to the trial balance first.

children.topic: Changing the books after sending them
children.note: Posting new journals after the auditor has the TB, without telling them, makes them test the wrong numbers.
Confirmations must go directly between the bank and the auditor. Your role is only to sign the authority letter.
Every journal needs a reason and a document. 'Adjustment' alone is not evidence.

children.topic: Leaving it all to the last week
children.note: Year-end chaos means missed accruals and cut-off errors. Reconcile monthly through the year.

children.topic: Q1: Find the bank statement balance
children.note: Cash book (adjusted) KES 250,000; unpresented cheques KES 40,000; uncredited deposits KES 15,000. What should the bank statement show?
Unpresented cheques have left the cash book but not the bank, so the bank is higher. Uncredited deposits are in the cash book but not yet in the bank, so the bank is lower.
On 1 October 2026 a firm paid KES 240,000 for 12 months' insurance and expensed it all. Year-end 31 December 2026. What is the adjustment?
240,000 ÷ 12 = KES 20,000 a month. Used: 3 months = 60,000. Prepaid: 9 months = 180,000.
Dr Prepayments KES 180,000 / Cr Insurance expense KES 180,000. Expense left for 2026 is KES 60,000.
Which ISA covers (a) bank confirmation letters and (b) the management representation letter?
(a) ISA 505 External Confirmations. (b) ISA 580 Written Representations.

nodeData.note: What to do when a KRA letter or audit arrives: stay calm, gather and reconcile your records, know the penalties, and answer or challenge findings the proper way. General guidance only, not legal or tax advice.

children.note: KRA (Kenya Revenue Authority) checks that the tax you declared matches what really happened in your business. A letter from KRA is serious, but it is not the end of the world. Calm, organised answers solve most cases.
KRA is the Government of Kenya agency that assesses, collects and accounts for the taxes and revenue due under Kenyan law.

manas.q: What does KRA do?

children.note: A tax audit (or compliance check) is KRA looking at your returns, books and records to see if you paid the right tax. It can be small (a few questions) or big (a full visit).

manas.q: What is a KRA tax audit?

children.note: Common reasons: your returns do not match other data KRA holds, big swings from year to year, refunds claimed, late or missing returns, or simply a random or sector check.
An audit is a check, not a finding of guilt. Many audits close with no extra tax, or with small corrections, when the records are good.
Extra tax, penalties and interest can add up fast. Quick, honest and well-documented replies keep costs low and protect your name.
This map is general guidance, not legal or tax advice. For a real dispute, or large sums, talk to a registered tax agent or an advocate.
KRA checks come in different sizes. Knowing which one you face helps you plan your reply.
KRA reviews your returns and documents from its office. You may be asked to send records or explanations by email or through iTax. No visit.

manas.q: What is a desk review?

children.note: KRA officers visit your premises to look at books, stock, systems and people. Usually wider and deeper than a desk review.

manas.q: What is a field audit?

children.note: KRA compares your iTax returns with eTIMS invoices, withholding certificates, customs data, bank and M-Pesa records and what your suppliers and customers declared.

manas.q: What is data matching in a KRA check?

children.note: A check on one tax or one item only, for example your VAT refund claim or your PAYE for one year.
A check across several taxes and several years: income tax, VAT, PAYE, withholding tax and more.
Sales on eTIMS higher than sales on the VAT return; input VAT claimed with no matching supplier invoice; payroll costs in the accounts with no PAYE return.
Read it, date it, and act the same week. Most trouble comes from ignoring a letter, not from the letter itself.
Note who sent it, which taxes and which periods it covers, what is asked for, and by when. Keep a copy in a single audit file.

manas.q: What four things should you note first in a KRA letter?

children.note: Confirm the letter through your iTax account or official KRA contact channels. Never pay money into a personal account or follow a link from an unknown sender.
KRA letters give dates for replies. The Tax Procedures Act sets strict deadlines for objecting and appealing — check them the day the letter arrives.

children.topic: Tell your accountant or tax agent
children.note: Bring in whoever prepares your returns at once. For a field audit or large amounts, get a registered tax agent or advocate on board early.
Choose one person to talk to KRA, so answers stay consistent and nothing is promised by mistake.

children.topic: Ask for more time in writing
children.note: If you cannot meet a date, ask in writing before it passes, explain why, and suggest a new date. Keep the reply.
Write down every call, email, meeting and document sent, with dates. This log protects you if there is a dispute later.
Before you answer, make sure your own numbers agree with each other. KRA will compare them anyway, so find the gaps first.
Sales and purchase invoices, eTIMS reports, bank and M-Pesa statements, payroll and P9s, contracts, withholding certificates, ledgers and filed returns.

manas.q: Name five records you should gather for a KRA check.

children.note: Line up each filed return with the general ledger for the same period. Sales, VAT, PAYE and withholding tax should agree or have a clear reason.

manas.q: What is the first reconciliation to do in a KRA check?

children.note: Total your eTIMS invoices for each month and compare with sales in the books. Look for missed, duplicated or cancelled invoices.

manas.q: Why compare eTIMS sales with the books?

children.note: Output VAT on sales minus input VAT on purchases should equal the VAT declared. Check each input VAT claim has a valid supplier invoice.
Money received should match sales plus loans, capital and other known receipts. Unexplained deposits are a common KRA question.
Salaries in the accounts should match the gross pay on the PAYE returns. Casual workers and allowances are often missed.
Write a short note for each gap: timing, a credit note, an error, or a non-taxable receipt. Attach the proof.
If you find a real mistake, it is usually better to correct it (and amend the return) than to hope KRA misses it. Ask your tax agent how.
KRA's penalties table sets out what each late filing, late payment or failure costs. Here are the main ones confirmed on kra.go.ke today.
Penalty is 25% of the tax due or KES 10,000, whichever is higher (check the current KRA rule, checked 27 Nov 2026).

manas.q: What is the penalty for late filing of PAYE?

children.note: Penalty is 5% of the tax due, plus interest of 1% per month on the unpaid tax (check the current KRA rule, checked 27 Nov 2026).

manas.q: What is the penalty for late payment of PAYE?

children.topic: Failure to withhold VAT or rental tax
children.note: Not deducting withholding VAT or withholding rental income tax costs 10% of the tax involved (check the current KRA rule, checked 27 Nov 2026).

manas.q: What is the penalty for failing to deduct withholding VAT?

children.note: Penalty is 5% of the tax due (check the current KRA rule, checked 27 Nov 2026).

manas.q: What is the penalty for late payment of withholding tax?

children.note: Monthly rental income (MRI) return filed late: 5% of the tax due or KES 2,000 for individuals (KES 20,000 for non-individuals), whichever is higher (check the current KRA rule, checked 27 Nov 2026).

manas.q: What is the late filing penalty for MRI returns?

children.note: Penalty is 5% of the tax due, plus interest of 1% per month (check the current KRA rule, checked 27 Nov 2026).
Penalty is 5% of the tax due or KES 10,000, whichever is higher (check the current KRA rule, checked 27 Nov 2026).

KRA has published guidelines on waiving penalties and interest under Section 89(5A) and (5B) of the Tax Procedures Act, Cap. 469B. Read the conditions on the KRA page and ask your tax agent (check the current KRA rule, checked 27 Nov 2026).

manas.q: Under which section can KRA waive penalties and interest?

children.note: Real numbers, step by step. Invented businesses only. Interest is worked as simple interest to keep it clear; check how KRA computes it on your own statement.
Baraka Hardware Ltd owed PAYE of KES 30,000 and paid it 3 months late.
Late payment penalty = 5% × 30,000 = KES 1,500.
Interest = 1% × 3 months × 30,000 = KES 900 (simple interest assumed).
Tax 30,000 + penalty 1,500 + interest 900 = KES 32,400 to pay.
Two cases show the 'whichever is higher' rule for late PAYE filing.
25% × 24,000 = KES 6,000. That is below KES 10,000, so the penalty is KES 10,000.
25% × 200,000 = KES 50,000. That is above KES 10,000, so the penalty is KES 50,000.
For small amounts the minimum KES 10,000 bites hard. File on time even if you cannot pay yet.

children.topic: Example 3: missed invoice in the books
children.note: Mama Njeri Supplies is checked by KRA. Its sales do not agree across three sources. VAT at 16% is used here (check the current KRA rate).
Sales per books KES 1,250,000. Sales per eTIMS KES 1,300,000. VAT return declared output VAT of KES 200,000 (16% × 1,250,000). All figures exclude VAT.
eTIMS 1,300,000 − books 1,250,000 = KES 50,000. Tracing shows one eTIMS invoice to a customer was never posted in the books.
Dr Trade receivables KES 58,000 / Cr Sales KES 50,000 / Cr VAT output KES 8,000 (16% × 50,000). Debits 58,000 = credits 58,000.
Correct output VAT = 16% × 1,300,000 = KES 208,000. Check: 200,000 + 8,000 = 208,000. Amend the return and pay the extra KES 8,000, plus any penalty and interest KRA charges.
Two landlords each file a monthly rental income return late with tax due of KES 15,000.
5% × 15,000 = KES 750. Below KES 2,000, so the penalty is KES 2,000.
5% × 15,000 = KES 750. Below KES 20,000, so the penalty is KES 20,000.
A client should have withheld KES 12,000 of VAT from a supplier's invoice but did not. Penalty = 10% × 12,000 = KES 1,200, on top of sorting out the tax itself.
After the check, KRA shares findings and may raise an assessment. You can agree, pay, or challenge it the proper way.
Reply point by point: agree, disagree with reasons, or explain. Attach evidence for each point. Keep it polite and factual.

manas.q: How should you answer KRA audit findings?

children.note: Accept and pay the items that are truly wrong. It shows good faith and stops more interest building up on them.
In general: KRA assessment → your objection to the Commissioner → the Commissioner's decision → appeal to the Tax Appeals Tribunal (TAT) → the High Court and higher courts.

manas.q: What is the order of steps in a Kenyan tax dispute?

children.note: A formal written challenge to an assessment, with reasons and documents, lodged with KRA (usually through iTax). The Tax Procedures Act sets strict deadlines for objecting and appealing — check them the day the letter arrives.

manas.q: What is a tax objection?

children.note: An independent tribunal that hears appeals against KRA decisions. Here a registered tax agent or advocate is strongly advised.

manas.q: What is the TAT?

children.note: Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) lets you settle a tax dispute with KRA outside the courts and the TAT (check the current KRA rule, checked 27 Nov 2026).

manas.q: What is ADR in Kenyan tax?

children.note: Three parties: the taxpayer, the Commissioner and a facilitator who helps both sides talk (check the current KRA rule, checked 27 Nov 2026).

manas.q: Who are the parties in KRA ADR?

children.note: Fill in the ADR application form, attach supporting documents and send them to the Tax Dispute Resolution Office, Ushuru Pension Towers, Nairobi (check the current KRA rule, checked 27 Nov 2026).
KRA lists the benefits as faster, cheaper, confidential and 'without prejudice', so talks cannot be used against you later (check the current KRA rule, checked 27 Nov 2026).

manas.q: Name the benefits of ADR.

children.note: Not where a deal would break the Constitution or revenue laws, the issue is a technical point of law, public interest needs a court ruling, undisputed judgments already exist, or a party will not engage (check the current KRA rule, checked 27 Nov 2026).
ADR has a 120-day timeline under Section 55 of the Tax Procedures Act (check the current KRA rule, checked 27 Nov 2026).

manas.q: How long does KRA ADR take under Section 55 TPA?

children.note: If you owe tax you cannot pay at once, ask KRA about paying in parts, and ask your tax agent whether a penalty and interest waiver applies.
Most audit pain is self-inflicted. Avoid these.
Silence lets dates pass. KRA can then raise an assessment on its own figures, which is much harder to undo.
Once the time to object or appeal passes, your options shrink. The Tax Procedures Act sets strict deadlines for objecting and appealing — check them the day the letter arrives.
A pile of receipts with no summary slows the audit and invites more questions. Send organised, labelled files with a short index.

children.topic: Books, eTIMS and iTax not agreeing
children.note: The most common finding. Reconcile monthly, not only when KRA calls.
Saying 'that was a loan' needs a loan agreement and bank proof. No document, no defence.
Rates and rules change. Always check the current KRA page before you calculate.

children.note: Use the 'whichever is higher' rule.
25% × 24,000 = 6,000, which is below 10,000. So the penalty is KES 10,000.
VAT at 16% (check the current KRA rate). What journal fixes the books?
Dr Trade receivables 46,400 / Cr Sales 40,000 / Cr VAT output 6,400. Debits 46,400 = credits 46,400.

nodeData.note: AI tools can save a working accountant hours on drafting, matching and sorting. But they guess, they can be wrong, and the accountant still signs off. This map shows what the tools are, good uses, the risks, and how to check the output.

children.topic: What AI is, in plain words
children.note: Artificial intelligence (AI) here means computer tools that read, write or sort information in a way that looks smart. They learn patterns from huge amounts of data. They do not understand your business the way you do.
Tools like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Microsoft Copilot. You type a question in plain words and they write an answer. They are good with words and ideas, weaker with exact numbers and current facts.

manas.q: What is an AI chat assistant?

children.note: It is built on a large language model (LLM): a program trained on lots of text that predicts the next likely words. That is why it sounds confident even when it is wrong.

manas.q: What is a large language model (LLM)?

children.note: Many cloud packages now suggest account codes, flag duplicates and draft reports for you. See 'Accounting software' earlier in this paper. The suggestion still needs your approval.
Copilot and similar helpers can write formulas, clean data and explain a sheet. Builds on 'Excel for accountants'. Always test the formula on a few rows you can check by hand.
You snap a photo of a receipt and the tool reads the supplier, date and amount. The reading part is called optical character recognition (OCR). Faded or handwritten receipts are often misread.

manas.q: What does OCR do for a bookkeeper?

children.note: The software pulls in bank or M-Pesa lines and suggests which invoice or bill each one pays. It matches on amount, date and name. Links to 'M-Pesa reconciliation'.

manas.q: What is bank-feed auto-matching?

children.note: The tool looks for odd items: a duplicate payment, a supplier paid twice, a round sum at midnight. It points, you investigate. It is a flag, not proof of fraud.

manas.q: What is anomaly detection?

children.note: A free public chat tool may keep what you type to improve itself. A business or enterprise version usually promises not to. Read the settings and terms before you use client data anywhere.

manas.q: How does a public AI tool differ from a business one?

children.note: Use AI for first drafts and first passes, where you can check the result quickly. Keep the final decision and the numbers in your own hands.
Ask for a polite reminder to a slow-paying customer or a memo to staff on a new petty cash rule. Then edit tone and facts. Ties to 'Credit control'.
Ask: 'Explain IAS 16 depreciation to a duka owner in five lines.' Good for learning and for explaining to clients. Then check against the real standard on the IFRS site.
Describe what you want: 'Sum column D where column B says Fuel.' It may give a SUMIFS formula. Test it on a small sample first.
It can pull out the key dates, amounts and penalty clauses from a long lease or supply contract. Read the clauses yourself before you rely on them.
Let the tool suggest matches between bank lines and the cash book. You approve each match and chase the leftovers. See the worked example below.
AI can suggest which account each receipt goes to: fuel, rent, staff welfare. It learns from your past choices, so early mistakes repeat. Review the first months closely.
Give it budget vs actual figures and ask for a short draft explaining the big differences. You add the real reasons, which only you know. Useful at 'Month-end close'.
A prompt is the instruction you type. Clear prompts give better answers.

manas.q: What is a prompt?

children.topic: Give a role and a goal
children.note: Start with 'You are an accounts assistant for a small Kenyan shop. I need…'. Context helps the tool pick the right level and style.
Ask for 'a table with columns Date, Payee, Amount, Suggested account' or 'five bullet points'. It is then easier to check.
Replace names, PINs and phone numbers with 'Customer A', 'Supplier 1'. You keep the shape of the problem without leaking data.
Say 'show each step of the calculation'. Then recompute the steps yourself. Hidden working hides errors.

children.topic: Ask what it is unsure of
children.note: Add 'list anything you are unsure about or that I should check'. It will not catch everything, but it helps.
AI saves time but brings new risks. The law, your professional body and your client all still hold you, not the tool, responsible.
A hallucination is when the AI states something false as if it were fact, such as an invented section of a law or a fake reference. It sounds just as sure when wrong.

manas.q: What is an AI hallucination?

children.note: Chat tools often give old or foreign tax rates and deadlines. Never take a rate from AI. Always check the current rate on the KRA website or iTax.

manas.q: Where must you confirm a Kenyan tax rate?

children.note: Many tools were trained up to a past date and may not know this year's Finance Act or new KRA rules. Ask yourself: could this have changed?
Never paste client records, payroll lists, patient data, ID numbers or KRA PINs into a public AI tool. Once sent, you cannot pull it back.

manas.q: What data should never go into a public AI tool?

children.note: This law controls how personal data about people is collected, stored and shared. The Office of the Data Protection Commissioner (ODPC) enforces it. Sending staff or customer data to an outside tool may break it.

manas.q: Which Kenyan law protects personal data?

children.note: ICPAK members follow a code of ethics based on the IESBA Code. Two key principles here: keep client information private (confidentiality) and only do work you can do well and check (professional competence and due care).

manas.q: Which two ethics principles matter most when using AI?

children.note: If AI gets a figure wrong and you sign it, the mistake is yours. Use professional judgement: ask whether the answer makes sense for this client.

manas.q: Who is responsible if AI gets a figure wrong?

children.note: ICPAK has said organisations taking up AI should look at who owns and governs it, whether the data is sound, whether the model is reliable, and whether its work can be audited.
In October 2026 AICPA & CIMA published new guidance on AI and the financial statement audit. Expect auditors to ask how AI was used in your records. See 'Preparing for an audit'.
Treat every AI answer as a draft from a new junior. Check it the same way you would check their work.
Add up totals yourself or in Excel. Check that debits equal credits. AI can make simple adding mistakes.

manas.q: What is the first check on any AI figure?

children.note: Match each item to the receipt, invoice, bank statement or M-Pesa statement. No document, no posting.

manas.q: What does 'tie to source' mean?

children.topic: Check law and rates at source
children.note: For tax, go to KRA. For standards, go to the IFRS site. For ethics, go to ICPAK. Do not trust a quoted section number until you have seen it.
Note what the AI suggested, who approved it and when. Good software logs this for you. An auditor or KRA officer may ask how a figure was made.

manas.q: What is an audit trail?

children.note: Ask: is this normal for this client? A fuel bill ten times last month's is a question, not a posting.
If AI categorised 300 receipts, check a sample of, say, 30, plus every large or unusual one. If you find errors, check more.
Two short cases from a small Nairobi hardware shop, Baraka Hardware. AI makes suggestions; the accountant checks and corrects them. All figures balance.

children.topic: Example 1: AI suggests a bank match
children.note: The bank feed shows a deposit of KES 34,800 on 12 Nov, narration 'MPESA PAYBILL J. MWANGI'. The tool suggests matching it to invoice INV-112 to Kamau Builders for KES 34,800.
Same amount, but the payer is J. Mwangi, not Kamau Builders. The ledger also has INV-118 to J. Mwangi for KES 34,800. The AI matched on amount only.
Reject the suggestion and match the deposit to INV-118. INV-112 stays unpaid and goes on the credit control list.
Dr Bank KES 34,800 / Cr Trade receivables – J. Mwangi KES 34,800. Debits 34,800 = Credits 34,800.
Same amount does not mean same customer. Always check name, reference and date, not just the figure.
After matching, the accountant prepares the reconciliation. Bank statement balance KES 412,600; cash book balance KES 398,050.

children.topic: Items the tool could not match
children.note: A deposit of KES 45,000 banked on 30 Nov not yet on the statement. Cheques of KES 62,300 written but not yet cleared. Bank charges of KES 2,750 not yet in the cash book.
Cash book KES 398,050 less bank charges KES 2,750 = KES 395,300. Journal: Dr Bank charges KES 2,750 / Cr Bank KES 2,750.
Bank statement KES 412,600 + deposit in transit KES 45,000 – unpresented cheques KES 62,300 = KES 395,300.
Both sides show KES 395,300, so the reconciliation balances. Keep the working with the bank statement in the month-end file.
The tool reads three receipts by OCR and suggests accounts: TotalEnergies KES 6,500 → Motor fuel; Naivas KES 4,200 → Office supplies; laptop KES 85,000 → Office expenses.
Fuel is right. The Naivas receipt shows tea, sugar and milk for staff, so it is Staff welfare. The laptop will be used for years, so it is a fixed asset, not an expense.
Dr Motor fuel 6,500; Dr Staff welfare 4,200; Dr Computer equipment 85,000 / Cr Bank 95,700. Debits 95,700 = Credits 95,700.
Correcting journal: Dr Staff welfare 4,200 / Cr Office supplies 4,200; and Dr Computer equipment 85,000 / Cr Office expenses 85,000. Add the laptop to the fixed asset register.
Fuel budget KES 60,000, actual KES 78,000. Over by KES 18,000, which is 18,000 ÷ 60,000 = 30%. AI drafts: 'Fuel is 30% over budget.'
AI cannot know that the van did extra deliveries to Kitengela this month. Add that reason and check the delivery log before sending to the owner.
A simple, low-risk way for a small Kenyan business to start with AI. Begin small, keep control, and grow once you trust it.
Start with something you can check fast, like drafting payment reminders or sorting receipts. Not tax returns.
Write one line: 'No client names, KRA PINs, ID numbers, payroll or patient data in public AI tools.' Share it with all staff.
Turn on the matching and receipt capture in the accounting software you already use. Your data stays in one system with a log.
For the first three months, a person approves every AI match and category. Note the mistakes it makes.
Do the normal month-end bank and M-Pesa reconciliation. If it does not agree, AI matching does not count as done.
A sheet with date, task, tool used, who checked it. This helps at audit time and if KRA asks questions.

children.topic: Q1: AI matches the wrong customer?
children.note: A KES 25,000 M-Pesa receipt from 'Achieng' is matched by AI to an invoice for 'Otieno Traders' of KES 25,000. What do you do?
Reject the match. Look for an open invoice to Achieng and check the M-Pesa reference.
Post Dr Bank (or M-Pesa) KES 25,000 / Cr Trade receivables – Achieng KES 25,000. Otieno's invoice stays open.
Bank statement KES 150,000; unpresented cheques KES 20,000; deposit in transit KES 8,000. Cash book KES 139,500; bank charges KES 1,500 not recorded. Does it agree?
139,500 – 1,500 = KES 138,000. Dr Bank charges 1,500 / Cr Bank 1,500. Both sides agree at KES 138,000.

children.topic: Q3: Can you paste the payroll?
children.note: Your manager asks you to paste the staff payroll, with names and KRA PINs, into a free chat tool to check PAYE. Should you?
No. It breaks confidentiality and may break the Data Protection Act 2019. Use payroll software or anonymised data, and check rates on the KRA site.

children.topic: Q4: AI gives a tax rate
children.note: A chat tool tells you a VAT rate and a filing deadline. What should you do before using them?
Treat both as unconfirmed. Check the current rate and deadline on kra.go.ke or iTax, and note where you checked.

nodeData.note: A plain guide to crypto for people already working: what it is, how to record it under IFRS, worked examples in KES, the records to keep and the scams to avoid. This is about accounting, not investment advice.

children.topic: What crypto is, in plain words
children.note: Crypto is a digital token that lives on a shared online record (a blockchain). Nobody like a bank or Safaricom sits in the middle; ownership is proved by a secret key.
A digital coin recorded on a blockchain, a shared database copied across many computers. Its price moves with supply and demand, often by a lot in one day.

manas.q: What is a cryptocurrency?

children.note: A shared digital ledger where each new block of transactions is chained to the last one. Once entries are confirmed they are very hard to change.

manas.q: What is a blockchain?

children.note: The first and best-known cryptocurrency, launched in 2009. Its supply is capped, and its price in KES can swing widely.
Coins designed to hold a steady value, usually 1 coin = 1 US dollar (for example USDT or USDC). They are still crypto and can lose their peg, so they are not cash.

manas.q: What is a stablecoin?

children.note: A general word for any digital unit on a blockchain. Some act like money, some give access to a service, some claim to be shares in a project.
A non-fungible token is one unique token, often linked to a picture or file. Each one is different, unlike coins where any one unit equals another.

manas.q: What is an NFT?

children.note: A wallet holds the keys that control your coins. The private key is like a PIN you can never reset: whoever has it controls the coins.

manas.q: What is a private key?

children.note: A wallet connected to the internet, such as a phone app or an exchange account. Easy to use but easier to hack.
A wallet kept offline, such as a hardware device or a paper backup locked in a safe. Safer for larger holdings.
Online platforms where you buy, sell and swap crypto for shillings or dollars. They charge fees and hold coins for many customers.
An M-Pesa balance is a claim to Kenya shillings, always worth KES 1 per shilling, and is usually treated like cash. Crypto has no fixed shilling value and no one promises to pay you back.

manas.q: How is crypto different from M-Pesa e-money?

children.note: The IFRS Interpretations Committee looked at this in June 2019 (agenda decision 'Holdings of cryptocurrencies'). The usual answer: an intangible asset, or inventory if you sell it as your trade.
Cash means money that is widely used to buy goods and to measure prices, like the shilling. Crypto is not used that way in practice, so it is not cash or a cash equivalent.

manas.q: Why is crypto not cash under IFRS?

children.topic: Why it is not a financial asset
children.note: A financial asset gives a contract right to receive cash, like a debtor or a bank deposit. Holding a coin gives no one the duty to pay you, so it is not a financial asset.

manas.q: Why is crypto not a financial asset?

children.note: Crypto is something you can identify and own but cannot touch, with no fixed shilling value. That fits IAS 38 Intangible Assets.
Record at cost (price plus direct fees). Each year-end, check for impairment and write down if value has fallen. No write-up above cost.

manas.q: What is the cost model for crypto under IAS 38?

children.note: If the recoverable amount is below carrying value, write it down and show the loss in profit or loss. A later price rise can reverse the loss, but only back up to original cost.

manas.q: Which standard covers crypto impairment?

children.note: Allowed only if there is an active market, such as a big exchange with daily prices. Rises go to a revaluation surplus in other comprehensive income (OCI); falls first reduce that surplus.

manas.q: When can crypto use the IAS 38 revaluation model?

children.note: Coins usually have an indefinite life, so they are not amortised. Instead you test for impairment at least once a year.
If you hold crypto to sell in the normal course of business, like a dealer, treat it as inventory under IAS 2 at the lower of cost and net realisable value.

manas.q: When is crypto inventory under IAS 2?

children.note: Commodity broker-traders who buy and sell to profit from short price moves may measure at fair value less costs to sell, with changes in profit or loss.

manas.q: How do commodity broker-traders measure crypto inventory?

children.note: IFRS 13 Fair Value Measurement tells you how to find a fair price: use the main market you can trade in, at the measurement date. Note the source and time you used.

manas.q: Which standard tells you how to measure fair value?

children.note: For comparison only: in the US, ASU 2023-08 measures most crypto at fair value through profit or loss. IFRS users in Kenya do not follow this.

manas.q: How does US GAAP (ASU 2023-08) measure crypto?

children.note: Notes should say which model you chose, the carrying amount, fair value if different, and any impairment. Auditors and readers need this.
Kenyan crypto rules have changed often. The points below were checked on 28 Nov 2026; always check the current rule before you rely on them.
The Finance Act 2023 brought a 3% Digital Asset Tax withheld by platforms. The Finance Act 2025 repealed it from 1 July 2025 (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What happened to Kenya's 3% Digital Asset Tax?

children.note: Since 1 July 2025 a 10% excise duty applies to the fees and commissions charged by virtual asset service providers (VASPs) (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What replaced the Digital Asset Tax from 1 July 2025?

children.note: Under the Finance Act 2026, virtual asset service providers must file an information return with KRA (check the current rule).
On 25 Nov 2026 KRA published draft Crypto Asset Reporting Framework and Common Reporting Standard regulations for comment by 8 Dec 2026. They are drafts, not yet law (check the current rule).

The Virtual Asset Service Providers Act, 2025 came into force on 4 Nov 2025. The CMA or CBK supervises, depending on the activity; CBK says licensing starts once regulations are in place (check the current rule).

manas.q: Who supervises VASPs in Kenya?

children.note: A profit on selling crypto may be income tax or capital gains tax, depending on the facts. Ask a tax adviser or check KRA guidance; we give no rate here.
Any crypto income or gains you must declare still go through the normal iTax return. See the earlier topic Filing on iTax.
Four short cases with Dr/Cr entries. Every entry is checked so debits equal credits.
Sokoni Traders buys 0.5 BTC for KES 4,000,000 and pays the exchange a fee of KES 20,000. The fee is a direct cost, so it is added to the asset.
Dr Crypto assets (intangible) KES 4,020,000 / Cr Bank KES 4,020,000.
Debits 4,020,000 = credits 4,020,000. Carrying amount is KES 4,020,000.
At 31 December the coins are worth KES 3,500,000 on the main exchange. Loss = 4,020,000 − 3,500,000 = KES 520,000.
Dr Impairment loss (profit or loss) KES 520,000 / Cr Accumulated impairment – crypto KES 520,000.
New carrying amount = 4,020,000 − 520,000 = KES 3,500,000. Debits equal credits at 520,000.
In March all 0.5 BTC is sold for KES 4,300,000, less a KES 15,000 fee, so the bank gets KES 4,285,000. Gain = 4,285,000 − 3,500,000 = KES 785,000.
Dr Bank 4,285,000; Dr Accumulated impairment 520,000 / Cr Crypto assets (cost) 4,020,000; Cr Gain on disposal 785,000.
A duka sells goods for KES 130,000 and the customer pays 1,000 USDT, worth KES 130,000 at that moment. Record the sale at that value.
Dr Crypto assets (intangible) KES 130,000 / Cr Sales revenue KES 130,000. VAT and eTIMS rules still apply (check the current rule).
The duka sells the 1,000 USDT for KES 129,500 and the exchange charges KES 500, so the bank gets KES 129,000.
Dr Bank 129,000; Dr Exchange fees 500; Dr Loss on disposal 500 / Cr Crypto assets 130,000.
A VASP charges a KES 1,000 trading fee plus 10% excise duty, KES 100 (check the current KRA rate). If you just pay fees, record KES 1,100 as fees.
Dr Exchange fees KES 1,100 / Cr Bank KES 1,100. If the fee is on a purchase, add it to the crypto cost instead.
A broker-trader holds coins at KES 600,000. At month-end fair value less costs to sell is KES 650,000, so record a KES 50,000 gain.
Dr Crypto inventory KES 50,000 / Cr Fair value gain (profit or loss) KES 50,000. Carrying amount is now KES 650,000.
Cost KES 1,000,000; fair value at year-end KES 1,200,000. Under revaluation the KES 200,000 rise goes to OCI, not profit.
Dr Crypto assets KES 200,000 / Cr Revaluation surplus (OCI) KES 200,000. Carrying amount KES 1,200,000.
Crypto can vanish with one wrong click, so records must be tight. Treat it like cash in a safe plus a fixed asset register.
List every wallet: its public address, which coins it holds, who controls it and whether it is hot or cold. Never list private keys here.

manas.q: What goes in a crypto wallet register?

children.note: Download monthly statements from each exchange showing buys, sells, fees and closing balances. Reconcile them to your ledger, like an M-Pesa reconciliation.
Keep keys and backup words offline, split between two trusted people where possible. Require two people to move large amounts.
For each transaction keep the date, time, coin, quantity, KES value, price source, fee and transaction ID (hash). Auditors can trace the hash on the blockchain.

manas.q: What should a crypto audit trail record?

children.note: Pick one exchange and one time (for example 23:59 EAT on the last day) and use it every period. Write the source down so the figure can be re-checked.

manas.q: Why record the valuation source and time?

children.note: Confirm wallet balances, reconcile exchange statements, update prices, book impairment, file evidence. See Month-end close.
Auditors will ask for wallet proofs and statements. See Preparing for an audit and When KRA audits you.
Many 'crypto investments' sold in Kenya and beyond are frauds. Accountants are often the first to spot the pattern.
No honest investment can promise fixed high returns like 'double your money in 30 days'. That is the classic sign of a Ponzi scheme.

manas.q: What is the top red flag of a crypto scam?

children.note: Early investors are paid with money from new investors, not from real profits. It collapses when new money stops.

manas.q: What is a Ponzi scheme?

children.note: If you earn mainly by signing up friends and family, it is a pyramid. Walk away.
Copy-cat websites and apps show fake balances and block withdrawals. Check the provider's licensing status with the CMA or CBK.
'Act today', 'don't tell your bank' or messages from strangers on WhatsApp are warning signs. Real deals can wait a day.
No real support agent needs your private key, seed words or M-Pesa PIN. Anyone asking is a thief.
Errors seen in real books and exam answers.
Crypto is not cash. Put it in intangible assets, or inventory for a dealer, not in cash and bank.
Under the cost model you cannot show a gain until you sell. Only the revaluation model (with an active market) or broker-trader rules allow it.
Purchase fees go into cost; selling fees reduce proceeds. Leaving them out gives the wrong gain.
A year-end value with no saved screenshot or export is hard to defend at audit.
The 3% Digital Asset Tax ended on 1 July 2025. Always check KRA's current position before filing.
